# egui-agent-chat

> An egui widget that shows a chat with an `agentai` agent. You create a `ChatPanel` with your
> own `agentai::Agent` and something that spawns tasks on your async runtime, then call
> `chat.ui(ui)` every frame. The widget streams answers in as Markdown, shows reasoning and
> tool calls as collapsible rows, and has an input with Send/Stop. For vision models it also
> sends images. The conversation is a plain `Vec<agentai::Message>`.

Key facts for integrating:

- `agentai` is not re-exported. Add it as your own dependency, from the `0.6` line this crate
  uses (0.5.0 or newer), so that both share one `Agent` type.
- This crate builds agentai without its default features; the TLS backend comes from your
  `agentai` dependency. Its defaults include `rustls-ring`. With `default-features = false`,
  turn on `rustls-ring`, `rustls-aws-lc` or `native-tls`, or HTTPS requests fail.
- The widget fills the `egui::Ui` it gets, including its own 12 px margins and an input panel
  at the bottom. To share the screen, put it in a side panel or a window.
- `ChatPanel::ui` returns the `ChatEvent`s of the frame: a turn started, finished, was stopped
  or failed, a tool was called or returned. Ignore them if you don't need them. The state is
  also readable at any time with `history()` and `is_running()`.
- A turn runs in the background. The widget asks egui for a repaint whenever data arrives, so
  you don't need to drive repaints yourself.
- A turn that is stopped or fails (e.g. cut off by the token limit while thinking) stays in
  the history with everything the agent wrote so far, reasoning included, marked "Stopped." or
  with the error. The conversation goes on from it; the history never rolls back and the
  prompt does not go back to the input. Only tool calls without a result are left out, as
  providers refuse them.
- Images are off by default. Turn them on with `set_capabilities` only when the model reads
  them.
- The agent can ask the user to choose (a form in the chat) through a tool you write: the chat
  shows a `Question` with `ask` and reports the answer as `ChatEvent::QuestionAnswered`; your
  code passes it back to the tool. See "Questions to the user".

## Install

```toml
[dependencies]
agentai = "0.6"
egui-agent-chat = "0.4"          # feature `tokio` is on by default
egui = "0.37"
eframe = "0.37"                  # or any other egui integration
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread"] }
egui_extras = { version = "0.37", features = ["all_loaders"] }  # to draw images
```

## Minimal integration (eframe + tokio)

```rust
use agentai::Agent;
use egui_agent_chat::ChatPanel;

struct App {
    chat: ChatPanel,
    // Keep the runtime alive as long as the chat; declare it after `chat` so it drops last
    _runtime: tokio::runtime::Runtime,
}

impl eframe::App for App {
    fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, _frame: &mut eframe::Frame) {
        self.chat.ui(ui);
    }
}

fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    // agentai picks the provider from the model name ("gpt-4.1-mini", "provider::model", ...)
    // and reads its settings from the environment, e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY. For a custom endpoint,
    // build an `agentai::genai::Client` and use `Agent::from_client(client, model, system)`.
    let agent = Agent::new("gpt-4.1-mini", "You are helpful.")?.with_max_iterations(12);
    let runtime = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?;
    let chat = ChatPanel::new(runtime.handle().clone(), agent);
    let app = App { chat, _runtime: runtime };
    eframe::run_native(
        "Chat",
        eframe::NativeOptions::default(),
        Box::new(|cc| {
            egui_extras::install_image_loaders(&cc.egui_ctx); // needed to draw images
            Ok(Box::new(app))
        }),
    )
    .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("{e}"))
}
```

## ChatPanel API

- `ChatPanel::new(spawner: impl Spawn, agent: impl Into<Arc<Agent>>) -> ChatPanel`: pass an
  `Agent`, or an `Arc<Agent>` that the rest of your app shares.
- `ui(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui) -> Vec<ChatEvent>`: call it every frame. It also takes in
  the data that streamed since the last frame, and returns what happened since then. See
  "Events".
- `ui_with_toolbar(&mut self, ui, add_widgets: impl FnOnce(&mut Toolbar<'_>)) -> Vec<ChatEvent>`:
  the same as `ui`, plus your own widgets on the left of the toolbar. Call one of the two each
  frame, not both. See "Custom toolbar widgets".
- `send(&mut self, ctx: &egui::Context, prompt: impl agentai::prompt::IntoPrompt)`: sends a
  message from code, with the current history. `prompt` is text or an `agentai::Prompt`, which
  may carry images. A running turn is stopped first, as with `cancel`. The input uses this
  method too.
  It does not check images against the capabilities.
- `cancel(&mut self)`: stops the running turn. The prompt and the reply so far stay in the
  history.
- `is_running(&self) -> bool`: whether the agent is working on an answer.
- `history(&self) -> &[agentai::Message]`: every ended turn, including the user's prompts.
- `set_history(&mut self, Vec<agentai::Message>)`: restores a conversation. It stops a running
  turn and clears the input. Pass `Vec::new()` to start a new chat.
- `set_input(&mut self, text: impl Into<String>)`: puts text into the input, e.g. a suggestion.
- `set_pending_context(&mut self, blocks: Vec<(String, String)>, label: Option<String>)`:
  context (title, body) for the next message, written or sent. See "Context blocks".
- `set_send_shortcut(&mut self, SendShortcut)`: picks the key combination that sends. See
  "Input behavior".
- `set_toolbar(&mut self, visible: bool)`: shows or hides the toolbar below the input, which
  holds the Send/Stop buttons. It is shown by default.
- `set_capabilities(&mut self, ModelCapabilities)`: says what the model can read. The default
  is text only. See "Images".
- `attach(&mut self, media: agentai::Media) -> bool`: attaches an image to the message being
  written. It returns `false` and drops the image when the capabilities don't allow it.
- `ask(&mut self, question: Question)`: shows a question form. See "Questions to the user".
- `dismiss_question(&mut self, id: &str)`: removes a question still waiting for an answer.
- `set_question_layout(&mut self, QuestionLayout)`: vertical (default) or horizontal choices,
  for questions without their own layout.

You can call any setter at any time, e.g. from your app's settings.

Configure the agent itself (system prompt, model, tools, max iterations) with `agentai`
before you pass it in. To change the agent, create a new `ChatPanel` and move the history
over with `set_history`.

## Events

`ui` and `ui_with_toolbar` return `Vec<egui_agent_chat::ChatEvent>`, in the order things
happened. The enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so match it with a `_` arm:

- `TurnStarted`: a turn started, from the input or from `send`.
- `ToolCalled(agentai::ToolCall)`: the agent called a tool.
- `ToolFinished { call_id, is_error }`: that tool returned, or failed.
- `TurnFinished`: the agent answered; the turn is in `history()`.
- `TurnStopped`: stopped with Stop, `cancel()`, or a new `send`; the turn so far is in
  `history()`.
- `TurnFailed { error }`: the turn failed with `error`; the turn so far is in `history()`.
- `QuestionAnswered { id, answer }`: the user answered the question `id` asked with `ask`.

Every turn starts with `TurnStarted` and ends with exactly one of the last three, except a
turn dropped by `set_history`, which ends without an event. Events of `send` or `cancel`
called outside `ui` come with the next frame.

```rust
for event in self.chat.ui(ui) {
    match event {
        ChatEvent::TurnFailed { error } => self.status = format!("Error: {error}"),
        _ => {}
    }
}
```

Code that passes `chat.ui(ui)` as the value of a closure that must return `()` needs a `;`:
`|ui| { chat.ui(ui); }`.

## Saving and restoring history

`agentai::Message` is serde-serializable, so you can store `chat.history()` and later pass it
back with `chat.set_history(saved)`. A good moment to save is when a turn ends:
`ChatEvent::TurnFinished`, `TurnStopped` or `TurnFailed { .. }`. After each of them the history
has grown.

## Images

Image support is behind the model capabilities, because a text-only model answers an image
with an error. Turn it on only for vision models:

```rust
use egui_agent_chat::ModelCapabilities;

chat.set_capabilities(ModelCapabilities::default().with_images(true));
```

With images on:

- The user can drop image files (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) on the window. On native platforms
  they are attached automatically. On the web, dropped files are not read yet.
- Your code can attach images with `chat.attach(media)`, or with `toolbar.attach(media)` from
  a toolbar button, e.g. with your own file picker. Build the image with
  `agentai::Media::from_bytes("image/png", bytes)`, and optionally `.with_name("cat.png")`.
- Attached images appear as thumbnails above the input, each with a remove button, and go with
  the next message, even one without text. Sent images appear in the user's bubble.
- `Toolbar::capabilities().images` tells your toolbar whether to show an image button.
- Turning images off with `set_capabilities` removes the images already attached.

To send an image from code without the input:
`chat.send(ctx, agentai::Prompt::text("What is in it?").with_image_bytes("image/png", &png))`.
Drawing images needs image loaders (`egui_extras::install_image_loaders`).

## Tools

Give the agent a toolbox with `agentai` (`Agent::with_toolbox`, the `#[toolbox]` macro, or
built-ins such as `agentai::tool::buildin::CurrentDateAndTimeToolBox`). The chat shows each
call as a row with the tool's name and a status (running / done / failed), its arguments as a
JSON tree, and the result. Images that a tool returns in its `agentai::tool::ToolOutput`
(`ToolOutput::from_text(..).with_media(media)`) appear below the call, and so do absolute
paths to existing PNG, JPEG or WebP files named in the result's text. This needs image loaders
(`egui_extras::install_image_loaders`).

## Questions to the user

The agent can ask the user to choose, e.g. what to do next. The chat draws the form; a tool you
write is the intermediary that asks and decides what the agent gets back.

```rust
use egui_agent_chat::{Answer, Choice, Question, QuestionLayout};

let question = Question::new(call.id.clone(), "Which **format**?", vec![
    Choice::text("png", "PNG"),
    Choice::image("photo", "Like this one", media), // an agentai::Media image
])
.with_multiple(true)           // checkboxes; the default is one choice with radio buttons
.with_other("Another format")  // a choice below the others, with a multi-line text field
.with_other_hint("Which one?") // a hint in that empty field; none by default
.with_declinable_label("None of them") // the decline button, "Skip" by default
// .with_declinable(false)     // no decline button
.with_image_size(egui::vec2(200.0, 200.0)) // the largest image size, 160×160 by default
.with_layout(QuestionLayout::Horizontal); // else the chat's `set_question_layout`
chat.ask(question);

for event in chat.ui(ui) {
    if let ChatEvent::QuestionAnswered { id, answer } = event {
        match answer {
            // ids of the chosen choices in the question's order, and the Other text
            Answer::Chosen { choices, other } => {}
            Answer::Declined => {}
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}
```

`Question`, `Choice` and `Answer` are `#[non_exhaustive]`: build them with their constructors
and `with_*` methods, and match `Answer` with a `_` arm.

The usual flow: a `#[toolbox]` tool takes a `call: &agentai::ToolCall` parameter (agentai
passes the call, it is not in the tool's schema), builds the `Question` with `call.id`, sends it
with a `futures_channel::oneshot::Sender<Answer>` over a `std::sync::mpsc` channel to the app,
calls `ctx.request_repaint()`, and awaits the oneshot. The app drains the channel each frame
before `ui` and calls `chat.ask`; on `QuestionAnswered` it sends the answer to the waiting tool,
which returns text for the agent, e.g. "The user chose: PNG". `examples/chat/ask.rs` in the
repository is a complete `ask_user` tool.

- With the id of a tool call, the form is drawn under that call. Once answered it shows the
  answer there, until `set_history`. A question with another id is drawn at the end of the
  chat and disappears once answered.
- A question of a tool call in the running turn goes away when the turn ends (Stop, an error,
  a new `send`); the tool is stopped with the turn. Others wait until answered or
  `dismiss_question`. `set_history` clears all. Asking with the id of a pending question
  replaces it.
- Choosing a picture or its checkbox/radio button both select it; the button next to it
  (accessibility label "Enlarge") shows the picture large in a modal, closed with Close, Esc or
  a click outside.
- Only the choices follow the layout. Other is always below them, with a multi-line text field
  that takes the rest of the width; writing in it chooses Other, and choosing Other focuses it.
- Submit is disabled until the answer is complete, and a note beside it says what is missing
  ("Choose an answer to submit", "Write your answer to submit").

## Context blocks

To attach long material (a file, a selection) to a prompt without flooding the chat, wrap it
with `egui_agent_chat::context_block(title, body)`. The model gets the full text, and the chat
shows it collapsed under its title.

```rust
let prompt = format!("{}\n\nSummarize it.", egui_agent_chat::context_block("notes.md", &notes));
chat.send(ui.ctx(), prompt);
```

`context_block_hidden(title, body)` writes `<context title="..." hidden>`: the model gets it,
the chat never draws it. A user message holding only hidden blocks (no text, no images) is
not drawn at all, e.g. for state your app sends the model on its own. Blocks are plain text
in the user `Message`, so a history you save and restore keeps them for the model.

`split_context(text)` does the reverse: it returns the blocks
(`ContextBlock { title, body, hidden }`) and the remaining text.

### Context for the user's next message

The input calls `send` itself, so your code can't change what the user typed. Instead call
`set_pending_context(blocks, label)` on any frame (it replaces what was set before; an empty
`Vec` sets none). The next `send`, from the input or your code, puts each (title, body) as
`context_block_hidden(title, body)` followed by a blank line before the prompt's text (before
everything if it has only images), then empties the list. The model gets the blocks; the chat
does not draw them, so the user's bubble shows only what they typed. `ChatEvent::TurnStarted` is your
sign that the context went. While it waits, `label` (e.g. `Some("Project changes will be sent
with your message".into())`) is shown dimmed over the input. `set_history` keeps it.

```rust
chat.set_pending_context(vec![("Project changes".to_owned(), diff)], None);
```

## Async runtimes

Turns run as `egui_agent_chat::Task` (a boxed `Send` future) through the `Spawn` trait.
Cancelling doesn't depend on the runtime: a stopped task is aborted.

- `tokio::runtime::Handle` (feature `tokio`, on by default): `runtime.handle().clone()`.
- Any closure `Fn(Task) + Send + Sync + 'static`, for other runtimes:
  `ChatPanel::new(move |task| { my_runtime.spawn(task); }, agent)`.
- `SmolGlobal` and `Arc<smol::Executor<'static>>` (feature `smol`). agentai's HTTP client
  needs a tokio reactor, so these implementations run each task through
  `async_compat::Compat`, which starts a small tokio runtime in the background.
- If you use your own closure on another runtime, wrap the task the same way:
  `move |task| { my_runtime.spawn(async_compat::Compat::new(task)); }`. Without that, requests
  panic with "there is no reactor running".

## Custom toolbar widgets

The toolbar below the input has Send/Stop on the right. Its left side is yours:

```rust
use egui_agent_chat::icons;

chat.ui_with_toolbar(ui, |toolbar| {
    // `toolbar` dereferences to the egui::Ui of the left side (laid out left to right)
    // An image button, only usable when the model reads images
    let images = toolbar.capabilities().images;
    let image_button = egui::Button::new(format!("{} Image", icons::IMAGE_PLUS));
    if toolbar.add_enabled(images, image_button).clicked()
        && let Some(path) = rfd::FileDialog::new().add_filter("PNG", &["png"]).pick_file() // any picker
        && let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(&path)
    {
        toolbar.attach(agentai::Media::from_bytes("image/png", bytes));
    }
    // A button that edits the message being written
    toolbar.add_enabled_ui(!toolbar.is_running(), |ui| {
        if ui.button("Summarize").clicked() { /* set your own app state */ }
    });
    if toolbar.button("Be brief").clicked() {
        toolbar.input().push_str(" Answer in one sentence.");
    }
});
```

- The closure runs every frame while the toolbar is shown. Add widgets and react to clicks in
  it, just like other egui code. It may borrow your app's state, because it is not stored.
- `Toolbar::input()` returns `&mut String`, the text in the input. `Toolbar::is_running()`
  says whether the agent is working on an answer.
- `Toolbar::attach(media) -> bool` attaches an image, and `Toolbar::capabilities()` tells
  whether the model reads images. See "Images".
- To send something yourself, set a flag in the closure, then call `chat.send(ctx, prompt)`
  after `ui_with_toolbar` returns. While it runs, the closure cannot borrow `chat`.
- `set_toolbar(false)` hides the whole toolbar, your widgets included. The closure then does
  not run.

## Icons

`egui_agent_chat::icons` holds the Lucide icon font that the widget uses. It installs itself
on the first frame. To use the icons elsewhere earlier, call `icons::install(ctx)`, then mix
the constants into text: `format!("{} Send", icons::SEND)`.

## Input behavior

`egui_agent_chat::SendShortcut` picks the key combination that sends. The other Enter
combinations add a line. Empty messages are never sent.

- `SendShortcut::Enter` (default), for mostly one-line messages: Enter sends, Shift+Enter
  adds a line.
- `SendShortcut::ShiftEnter`, for mostly multi-line messages: Shift+Enter sends, Enter adds a
  line.
- `SendShortcut::Custom(egui::KeyboardShortcut)`, e.g.
  `KeyboardShortcut::new(Modifiers::COMMAND, Key::Enter)` for Cmd/Ctrl+Enter. Enter adds a
  line.

The placeholder in the empty input names the current shortcuts. While the agent runs, the
toolbar's Send button becomes Stop. If you hide the toolbar with `set_toolbar(false)`,
messages are sent only with the shortcut, and only `cancel()` stops an answer. Give your
users another way to stop, e.g. a menu item.
